auto_run_disabled.description: Indicates whether full syncs are paused for this connector
auto_run_disabled.rationale: Controls whether automatic full synchronisation runs. This affects operational behaviour rather than access control, encryption, authentication, or other security properties.

collection_display_name.description:
The display name of the Collection.
Should be human readable, used to display collections in the Console
Dashboard. UTF-8 encoded string with limit of 1024 characters.
collection_display_name.rationale: Human-readable display name for the collection. Cosmetic metadata with no security effect, so it is not a policy target.

collection_id.description:
The ID to use for the Collection, which will become the final component
of the Collection's resource name. A new Collection is created as
part of the DataConnector setup. DataConnector is a singleton
resource under Collection, managing all DataStores of the Collection.
This field must conform to [RFC-1034](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc1034)
standard with a length limit of 63 characters. Otherwise, an
INVALID_ARGUMENT error is returned.
collection_id.rationale: Identifier referencing a collection. We do not constrain resource identifiers or references to other resources.

connector_modes.description:
The modes enabled for this connector. The possible value can be:
'DATA_INGESTION', 'ACTIONS', 'FEDERATED'
'EUA', 'FEDERATED_AND_EUA'.
connector_modes.rationale: Controls which connector capabilities are enabled. DATA_INGESTION imports data, ACTIONS performs connector actions, FEDERATED enables federated search, EUA enables end-user authentication, and FEDERATED_AND_EUA combines federated search with end-user authentication. Because the field may be empty or use an unspecified default, an explicit allowlist prevents accidental activation of privileged workflows and restricts the connector to approved least-privilege modes.

data_source.description:
The identifier for the data source.
This is a partial list of supported connectors. Please refer to the
[documentation](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/connectors/introduction-to-connectors-and-data-stores)
for the full list of connectors.

Supported first-party connectors include:

*   'bigquery'
*   'gcp_fhir'
*   'google_mail'
*   'google_drive'
*   'google_calendar'
*   'google_chat'

Supported third-party connectors include:
Generally available (GA) connectors:

*   'onedrive'
*   'outlook'
*   'confluence'
*   'jira'
*   'servicenow'
*   'sharepoint'

Preview connectors:

*   'asana'
*   'azure_active_directory'
*   'box'
*   'canva'
*   'confluence_server'
*   'custom_connector'
*   'docusign'
*   'dropbox'
*   'dynamics365'
*   'github'
*   'gitlab'
*   'hubspot'
*   'jira_server'
*   'linear'
*   'native_cloud_identity'
*   'notion'
*   'okta'
*   'pagerduty'
*   'peoplesoft'
*   'salesforce'
*   'shopify'
*   'slack'
*   'snowflake'
*   'teams'
*   'trello'
*   'workday'
*   'zendesk'
data_source.rationale: Identifier naming the connector/data source the data store pulls from (e.g. bigquery, google_mail). This is a reference to another resource/system chosen by the team; we do not constrain what a resource points at.

data_source_version.description: The version of the data source. For example, '3' for Jira v3.
data_source_version.rationale: Specifies the connector API version. Version selection is a compatibility concern rather than a configurable security control.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform can delete or abandon the resource. Preventing accidental deletion is an important governance and security control.

incremental_refresh_interval.description:
The refresh interval specifically for incremental data syncs. If unset,
incremental syncs will use the default from env, set to 3hrs.
The minimum is 30 minutes and maximum is 7 days. Applicable to only 3P
connectors. When the refresh interval is
set to the same value as the incremental refresh interval, incremental
sync will be disabled.
incremental_refresh_interval.rationale: Determines how frequently incremental synchronisation occurs. This is an operational scheduling setting rather than a security control.

incremental_sync_disabled.description: Indicates whether incremental syncs are paused for this connector.
incremental_sync_disabled.rationale: Enables or disables incremental synchronisation. This affects data freshness rather than security.

json_params.description: Params needed to access the source in the format of json string.
json_params.rationale: Free-form JSON string of connection params used to reach the source. The content is team/connector-specific and cannot be meaningfully constrained by a generic platform policy, so it is out of scope (free-form document).

kms_key_name.description:
The KMS key to be used to protect the DataStores managed by this connector.
Must be set for requests that need to comply with CMEK Org Policy
protections.
If this field is set and processed successfully, the DataStores created by
this connector will be protected by the KMS key.
kms_key_name.rationale: Specifies the Cloud KMS key used to encrypt managed data stores. Requiring kms_key_name to be non-empty ensures that a customer-managed encryption key is configured for data protection without constraining any team-specific project, region, key-ring, or key identifier.

location.description:
The geographic location where the data store should reside. The value can
only be one of "global", "us" and "eu".
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

params.description: Params needed to access the source in the format of String-to-String (Key, Value) pairs.
params.rationale: Free-form map of string key/value params used to reach the source. The content is connector/team-specific and cannot be meaningfully constrained by a generic policy, so it is out of scope.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Project the resource belongs to. This is an identifier/reference and is not a security policy target.

refresh_interval.description:
The refresh interval for data sync. If duration is set to 0, the data will
be synced in real time. The streaming feature is not supported yet. The
minimum is 30 minutes and maximum is 7 days. When the refresh interval is
set to the same value as the incremental refresh interval, incremental
sync will be disabled.
refresh_interval.rationale: How often the connector refreshes data from the source. This is a data-management scheduling choice for the team, not a security control.

static_ip_enabled.description: Whether customer has enabled static IP addresses for this connector.
static_ip_enabled.rationale: Determines whether static IP addresses are used for connector communication. Network exposure and firewall allow-listing make this security relevant.

sync_mode.description:
The data synchronization mode supported by the data connector. The possible value can be:
'PERIODIC', 'STREAMING'.
sync_mode.rationale: Selects the synchronisation method (periodic or streaming). This is an operational configuration rather than a security control.

action_config.description:
Action configuration for the data connector. Configures action
capabilities for connectors that support the ACTIONS connector mode.

action_config.action_params.description:
Params needed to configure the actions in the format of
String-to-String (Key, Value) pairs. Contains connection
credentials and configuration for the action connector.
action_config.action_params.rationale: Contains connector-specific free-form action parameters that may include operational or credential values. A generic platform policy cannot meaningfully interpret or validate this arbitrary configuration.

action_config.create_bap_connection.description:
Whether to create a BAP (Business Application Platform) connection
for this action connector.
action_config.create_bap_connection.rationale: Determines whether a Business Application Platform connection is provisioned. This is an architectural integration choice rather than a generic platform security control.

bap_config.description:
BAP (Business Application Platform) configuration for the data
connector. Controls which actions are enabled for connectors
using the ACTIONS connector mode.

bap_config.enabled_actions.description:
The list of enabled actions for this connector. Supported
values include: 'create_issue', 'update_issue',
'change_issue_status', 'create_comment', 'update_comment',
'upload_attachment'.
bap_config.enabled_actions.rationale: Selects the application-specific integration actions enabled for the connector. This is feature configuration determined by the application team rather than a generic platform security policy target.

bap_config.supported_connector_modes.description:
The connector modes supported by the BAP configuration.
The possible values include: 'ACTIONS'.
bap_config.supported_connector_modes.rationale: Lists supported connector modes. This is descriptive metadata rather than an enforceable security setting.

destination_configs.description:
Destination connector configurations for the data connector,
used to configure where data is served.

destination_configs.key.description: The key of the destination configuration, for example 'url'.
destination_configs.key.rationale: Identifies the destination configuration entry. It is metadata and does not directly affect security.

destination_configs.params.description: Additional parameters for this destination config in structured json format.
destination_configs.params.rationale: Contains destination-specific configuration. The values are connector-specific and cannot be validated through a generic platform security policy.

destination_configs.destinations.description: The list of destinations for this configuration.

destination_configs.destinations.host.description:
The host of the destination, for example
'https://example.atlassian.net'.
destination_configs.destinations.host.rationale: Specifies the external destination host used by the connector. Destination endpoints are application-specific references, and a generic platform policy does not pin particular hosts or destinations.

destination_configs.destinations.port.description: Target port number accepted by the destination.
destination_configs.destinations.port.rationale: Defines the destination network port. Restricting ports reduces unnecessary network exposure.

entities.description: List of entities from the connected data source to ingest.

entities.entity_name.description:
The name of the entity. Supported values by data source:
* Salesforce: 'Lead', 'Opportunity', 'Contact', 'Account', 'Case', 'Contract', 'Campaign'
* Jira: project, issue, attachment, comment, worklog
* Confluence: 'Content', 'Space'
entities.entity_name.rationale: Specifies which entity type is synchronised. This is an application configuration choice rather than a security control.

entities.key_property_mappings.description:
Attributes for indexing.
Key: Field name.
Value: The key property to map a field to, such as 'title', and
'description'. Supported key properties:
* 'title': The title for data record. This would be displayed on search
  results.
* 'description': The description for data record. This would be displayed
  on search results.
entities.key_property_mappings.rationale: Maps source fields to index properties. This affects indexing behaviour but not security.

entities.params.description: The parameters for the entity to facilitate data ingestion.
entities.params.rationale: Contains entity-specific configuration parameters. These are application-specific and outside the scope of generic security policy.
